what_happened: Dispatch says def:interval-site, def:twisted-arrow and lem:interval-twisted-arrow are commented out inside a SECTION CUT block in JPL/possible_worlds.tex. They are no longer in that file at all: the whole cut block was relocated to JPL/appendix_cut_material.tex (grep of possible_worlds.tex returns no def:interval-site). Verbatim statements were read from the relocated file instead. Also the task-111 report path in the dispatch is stale: it now lives under specs/archive/111_verify_interval_twisted_arrow_lemma/.

Whole module prototyped end-to-end in lean_run_code during research: duration monoid laws, Factorization category with both linear-preorder halves, Tw category with all three category laws, the hom-set bijection in both directions, functoriality, and both coverage-transport equations all compile with zero sorries and NO new import beyond FormalSystem.Semantics.Presheaf.Site. Implementation is transcription, not discovery.

Declared file_scope names only FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Duration.lean, but landing the module unavoidably requires edits to four files outside it: FormalSystem.lean (C33 requires byte-exact mk_all output), FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf.lean (aggregator import, the shared touch the dispatch already flags), docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md (C15 is enforced and def:twisted-arrow / lem:interval-twisted-arrow / lem:factorization-linear have no row), and FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/README.md (module table convention). Only the aggregator was anticipated.

The research report prototyped every deliverable declaration end to end in compiled probes (zero sorry, [propext] footprints, tactic survey per goal), so planning reduced to transcribing a verified shape into four phases; the Lean Challenge Statements block was typechecked against the live tree in one lean_run_code call with only sorry warnings.

lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check resolves pinned identifiers tree-wide by BARE name (regex theorem|lemma|def|instance NAME, no namespace), so a plan whose module mirrors Site.lean's Tr.comp/Tr.id/Tr.ext naming inside new namespaces (Dur, Tw) is guaranteed an exit-71 'resolves to more than one declaration' on --check regardless of naming choices, since Site.lean already declares those bare names. Worked around by recording the limitation in the plan's Risks and verifying statement fidelity via lean_hover_info against the pinned block; the tool would need namespace-aware resolution to be useful on a tree this size.

Phase 1's declared check (check-module-invariants.sh --no-build exits 0) cannot be met in isolation: the three new DANGLING rows name FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Duration.lean as the Lean counterpart, exactly as the sibling def:interval-site row names Site.lean, and C12 fails that path as unresolved because Phase 2 creates the file. C15's row-before-citation rule orders the row first; C12's live-path rule orders the file first. C15 itself passes (88 citations resolve). Resolution: close Phase 1 with the exit-0 criterion recorded as a reasoned exclusion evidenced by the four C12 lines, and re-run the --no-build harness at Phase 2 end to observe C12 green once the module exists.

Phase 2's verification note expected every part-A theorem at most [propext]. Measured with lean_verify: Factorization.ext, hom_unique, fst_le and Dur.comp_assoc are [propext]; homOfLe, ofCut, hom_total and ofCut_fst_self are [propext, Quot.sound]. Localized to Mathlib's sub_nonneg, which Site.lean's coverRight (and even Tr.comp_assoc) already carry at the identical [propext, Quot.sound]. The criterion that matters -- no Classical.choice, which the commuted add_left_cancel was chosen to secure -- holds for every declaration; the plan's bar was simply tighter than the module's own baseline. Recorded in the plan and README as choice-free with the measured sets, no proof changed.

The Phase 2 commit was refused by the repository pre-commit hook (scripts/typst-sync-check.sh Check 2): typst/generated/status.typ records the FormalSystem file count (709) and line count, and adding Duration.lean moved both. Neither the plan's Files-to-modify lists nor the research's gate-by-gate companion-file table named this file; the research's own Context Extension Recommendation (a new-module checklist) would have caught it. Remedy applied as the hook prescribes: bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix, with typst/generated/status.typ staged alongside the phase's files. Every later phase that changes the module's line count will need the same regeneration before its commit.

Both halves of Duration.lean compiled green on the first scoped build with zero warnings and zero sorries, and both transport theorems closed by ext; rfl with the elaborated term Tr.ext (Eq.refl _) -- no cast. The research report's compiled end-to-end probe made implementation a transcription, exactly as the plan predicted; the only in-phase adjustments were docstring wording.
